introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2025. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub mark in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH paper are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

Calculators are Allowed.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) On the outline Map of Cameroon provided, locate and name the following:

(i) A named area of high population density in the North region,
(ii) The Limbe refinery,
(iii) The Kimbi forest reserve,
(iv) The Lagdo dam,
(v) A named area with Sudan vegetation.

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each item is worth one mark: the name must be written on the map and the mark (a cross or a dot) must be in the correct part of the country. Use the outline map above (north at the top; the Atlantic coast and the border with Nigeria are on the west side, the borders with Chad and the Central African Republic on the east, and the southern border on the bottom edge).

| Item | Where to mark and name it |
|---|---|
| (i) Area of high population density in the north | The **Mandara Mountains and the Maroua area (Diamare plain)** in the Far North, in the north of the country at the narrow northern part of the outline. (Garoua and the Benue valley are accepted as another densely settled area in the north.) |
| (ii) The Limbe refinery | **Limbe** (the SONARA refinery), on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea at the foot of Mount Cameroon in the South-West Region, in the extreme west of the country near the coast. |
| (iii) The Kimbi forest reserve | **Kimbi** (the Kimbi reserve), in the North-West Region near the border with Nigeria and on the west side of the country. |
| (iv) The Lagdo dam | On the **River Benue** at Lagdo, upstream of Garoua in the North Region, in the north of the country. |
| (v) An area with Sudan vegetation | The **Benue plains around Garoua** in the North Region (Sudan savanna: grass with scattered thorny and drought-resistant trees, between the Adamawa plateau and the Sahel-type vegetation of the Lake Chad area). |

(Other correct examples are accepted when they are correctly placed.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) Describe **THREE** measures taken by government to improve livestock farming in Cameroon.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three measures (2 marks each: the measure and its description):

1. **Animal health services.** The Ministry in charge of livestock (MINEPIA) organises veterinary posts and vaccination and disease-control campaigns against diseases such as anthrax and foot-and-mouth disease, and the treatment of animals against parasites, which reduces losses of animals.
2. **Research and improvement of breeds and pasture.** Livestock research and breeding stations (for example the Wakwa station near Ngaoundere in the Adamawa) produce improved breeds, by cross-breeding and artificial insemination, and improved pasture, and give them to farmers.
3. **Training, extension and support to farmers.** Government agents train herders and give advice, and the State and its partners give credit or grants for the purchase of animals, feed and equipment, and create water points, ranches, and cattle markets and slaughterhouses to improve the marketing of animals.

(Other accepted measures: the control of transhumance and the sharing of grazing land between herders and farmers, the building of cold stores, and the encouragement of poultry, pig and fish farming.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) (i) Explain **THREE** ways by which food loss can be reduced.
(ii) State **THREE** impacts of agriculture to the economy.

(6+3=9 marks)

Total (20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three ways of reducing food loss (6 marks, two marks each: the way and its explanation).**

1. **Better storage.** Granaries, silos, warehouses and solar dryers that are clean, dry and protected against rats, insects and moulds keep the harvest from rotting after it has been harvested.
2. **Processing and preservation.** Drying, smoking, salting, canning and the use of cold stores and refrigerated vehicles turn perishable foods (fish, meat, fruits, vegetables, tubers) into products that last longer and can be sold when the price is higher.
3. **Better roads, transport and markets.** Good feeder roads, suitable vehicles and organised markets get the produce quickly from the farm to the buyers before it spoils; training farmers in good harvesting and handling, and in pest control, further reduces the losses.
4. Another way: reducing waste in shops and homes (buying only what is needed, using leftovers, selling the imperfect produce).

**(ii) Three impacts of agriculture on the economy (3 marks, one mark each).**

1. It **gives employment and income** to a large proportion of the population, especially in rural areas.
2. It **provides food** for the population (food security) and **raw materials** for industry (cotton for textiles, sugar cane for sugar, cocoa and coffee for processing).
3. It **earns foreign exchange and government revenue** from the export of cash crops such as cocoa, coffee, bananas and cotton, and it makes up an important part of the Gross Domestic Product.
